subject: Reconciling Nov renewal surge — proposed one‑off makeup
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme-corp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts-payable@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected Feb–Mar surge after renewal — need reconciliation

Hi Dylan,

Hope you're well. We completed our renewal with Redwood on 2026-02-01 (new term: 12 months) but our engineering team discovered a sustained spike in Feb–Mar that pushed us well past our committed capacity. The usage export attached to this email shows the token-hours and model variants in question.

Billing shows a one‑time overage posted to our account for $24,600; before we close the month we need to reconcile how that number was calculated. Two quick asks:
- Can you send the internal usage / trace that ties those high-inference runs to the committed bucket?
- We'd like to propose splitting any agreed one‑time credit across the next two invoices rather than a single refund.

We can make time Thursday morning PST for a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Corp
attachments: acme_febmar_usage_export.csv (CSV, 425KB)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, accounts-payable@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 12:30:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb–Mar surge after renewal — need reconciliation

Maya — thanks for the detail and the export. Appreciate the heads up.

Quick summary from our side after a first-pass review:
- We see two long-running async inference jobs (2026-02-18 and 2026-03-04) that used a higher-rate model variant than what's in your committed profile; those account for ~72% of the spike.
- The $24,600 overage is the sum of the incremental per-token charges for those sessions, plus the burst surcharge for sustained concurrency.

I've attached our proposed one‑off invoice (dylan_oneoff_invoice_v1.pdf) that reconciles the raw consumption, and a CSV with the filtered traces that map to the invoice rows. Suggested options:
A) One‑time credit of 60% of the overage applied immediately (refund or credit)
B) Split credit across next two invoices (50%/50%), applied as negative line items

If you'd like, Marcus (cc'd) can approve a partial credit today and we can route a PO to billing to finalize. I'm available Thursday 9–11am PST to talk through the traces live.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: dylan_oneoff_invoice_v1.pdf (PDF, 112KB)
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme-corp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts-payable@acme-corp.com, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:07:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb–Mar surge after renewal — need reconciliation

Thanks Dylan — and thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple of clarifying points from our finance and engineering teams:

- The two long-running jobs you flagged were orchestrated by a partner integration; we accept that those runs were higher than expected, but we believe a portion (approx 20%) should be excluded because they were duplicate replays initiated during an incident.
- Instead of a single immediate credit, we'd prefer the split-credit approach across two invoices — that helps our cashflow planning.

Can you do a second-pass with the trace IDs we've flagged (see column "replay_flag" in the CSV)? If you can confirm exclusion of the duplicates we'll accept a 50% credit up front and 50% on the following invoice. Also — please add line-item detail in the invoice showing the excluded runs so our AP team can match against the PO.

If it's easier, we can sign off on the PO now and have AP route payment when the net invoice hits.

Best,
Maya
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme-corp.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, accounts-payable@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb–Mar surge after renewal — need reconciliation

Maya — thanks for the note and for flagging the replay IDs. I've reviewed the trace CSV Dylan sent and the replay_flag column. We agree to exclude the flagged replay runs (approx 20% of disputed consumption) from the overage calculation.

Approved resolution:
- Adjusted overage after excluding replays = $19,680 (updated invoice attached).
- Apply a makeup credit equal to 50% of the adjusted overage on ACME invoice 20261115; remaining 50% to be applied on invoice 20261215.
- Redwood will send a revised invoice with line-item detail and a PO-friendly description.

Next steps required from Acme: please confirm PO number to reference on the revised invoice and confirm that AP will accept the split-credit schedule. Once confirmed, billing will issue the revised invoice and we can route a DocuSign for the PO if you prefer.

Reference: DEAL-2026-ACME-4321 — Marcus Lin (Sales Lead) has approved a one-off credit per the schedule above.

- Marcus
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts-payable@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb–Mar surge after renewal — need reconciliation

Marcus / Dylan — this works for us. AP will issue PO ACME-PO-78844 and accept the split-credit schedule. I've attached the signed PO for your records. Please include the PO number on the revised invoice and send the DocuSign link for the credit agreement if required.

We'll schedule a short post-mortem with our infra team to avoid duplicate replays in the future. Thanks for moving quickly on this.

Maya Singh
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Corp
